headline: Focus is directing attention deliberately—the ability to choose what gets your mental resources
universal_truth: Attention is your most valuable resource; where you direct it determines what you create
fun_facts: It takes an average of 23 minutes to fully regain focus after an interruption
Multitasking is a myth—the brain switches between tasks, losing efficiency with each switch
Deep focus activates 'flow states' where people do their best work and feel most alive
discussion_questions: What steals your attention most often?
When do you experience deep focus?
What would you create with better focus?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Your attention is finite. Every notification, every distraction, every wandering thought costs you. In a world designed to capture your attention, the ability to direct it deliberately is a superpower. Focus is freedom.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We're more distracted than ever—phones, notifications, endless content. But distraction isn't new; minds always wander. What's changed, and how can we reclaim focus?

options.text: Focus improves by reducing external distractions, training attention through practice, and creating environments that support concentration
options.response: Yes. Focus is both environmental and trainable. Remove distractions, practice sustained attention, and design your space for concentration. Focus is a skill you can build.

options.text: Some people naturally focus better than others
options.response: Natural differences exist, but focus is highly trainable...

q1.title: Attention Residue
q1.script: When you switch tasks, part of your attention stays on the previous task—'attention residue.' It takes about 23 minutes to fully re-engage. Every switch costs you. Protect blocks of uninterrupted time for deep work.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Attention Residue"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Environment Design
q2.script: Willpower is limited; environment is powerful. Put your phone in another room. Use website blockers. Create a physical space associated with focus. Make distraction hard and focus easy.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Attention Training
q3.script: Focus is like a muscle—it strengthens with use. Meditation trains attention explicitly. Deep work sessions extend capacity. Start with short focus periods and gradually lengthen them. The more you practice, the longer you can sustain.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Attention is your most valuable resource. Focus teaches that where you direct attention determines what you create. Guard it jealously.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 187. Tomorrow, we'll explore keeping going when it's hard—persistence. Until then, try one focused work session with all distractions removed.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Focus Session - Remove and Concentrate
growTrack.activity: Do one 25-minute focus session today: phone away, notifications off, single task only. Notice how it feels. Notice when your mind wanders. Notice what you accomplish. This is the Pomodoro technique—and it works.
